# Feature: a hub master for the online play table (owner decision 2026-10-28)

Repository: claude-code-game-master (the hub copy of the owner's laptop repo, synced by Mutagen; edit files directly with Edit/Write).
Commands like `uv run pytest` run on the laptop automatically (the hub forwards them); just run them from the repo root.
Do NOT commit, push, deploy, ssh anywhere, touch the VPS, or create T3 threads/tasks. Code + tests + docs only.

## Background (read the code before changing it)
- `backend/screen_driver.py` runs one online table (DM_PLAY_TABLE = play|demo) as systemd unit `dnd-play@<table>`
  (`ops/play/dnd-play@.service`, sandboxed: AppArmor profile, ProtectHome=tmpfs + BindPaths, NoNewPrivileges).
  It collects player actions from the screen inbox and sends each batch as one message to a Claude Agent SDK master
  (`backend/providers/claude_screen.py`, Sonnet 5.5, full Claude Code in the repo). The master publishes a turn with
  `bash tools/dm-screen.sh turn --file <json|->`; the driver checks `turn_id(sdir)` grew. See `play()`, `send()`,
  `_consume()`, follow-up logic, caps, usage-limit carry. Tests: `tests/test_screen_driver.py` (FakeProvider, Table, FakeClock).
- The SDK master gets a PostToolUse hook (`python3 -m lib.screen.cli hook`, `lib/screen/cli.py run_hook`) that puts dice
  rolls etc. into the live feed and prints a Claude Code additionalContext "act nudge" (`lib/screen/hook.py act_nudge`).
- The master contract: `.claude/additional/infrastructure/screen-driver-contract.md` (forbidden commands listed there).

## Goal
The owner's table (play) can be played by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent in a T3 thread on the "hub" server instead of the SDK master.
The driver POSTs each batch to a T3 webhook URL; the hub agent then runs engine tools on the VPS through
`ssh kesha@VPS` with a restricted key whose forced command is a root-owned gate; the gate forwards each call over a unix
socket to the table's driver, which runs the tool INSIDE the table's sandbox (never outside it: the sandboxed SDK masters can
edit repo files, so the gate must never execute repo code itself). If the hub master has not published a turn within
DM_PLAY_HUB_TIMEOUT (300 s) the driver revokes the turn's ticket and the SDK master (Sonnet on the VPS) plays that batch;
the next batch goes to the hub again (after DM_PLAY_HUB_FAILS=2 consecutive hub failures the hub is skipped for
DM_PLAY_HUB_PAUSE=900 s). The demo table stays SDK-only (default mode).

1. Settings from env (dataclass, like `Settings`): DM_PLAY_MASTER ("hub" or "sdk", default "sdk"; anything else -> sdk + warning),
   DM_PLAY_HUB_WEBHOOK (URL; the driver pops it from os.environ at start so the SDK CLI child never inherits it; never log it,
   log only "set"/"unset"), DM_PLAY_HUB_TIMEOUT=300, DM_PLAY_HUB_FAILS=2, DM_PLAY_HUB_PAUSE=900, socket path
   DM_PLAY_HUB_SOCKET or "$RUNTIME_DIRECTORY/hub.sock" (systemd sets RUNTIME_DIRECTORY). Hub mode without a webhook or a socket
   location: log an error and run as sdk.
2. post_event(url, payload, timeout=20) -> (ok, error): stdlib urllib POST of JSON (Content-Type application/json), 2xx = ok.
   Error text must not contain the URL (it holds a token​).
3. HubBridge: asyncio unix-socket server (asyncio.start_unix_server). Unlink a stale socket, bind, chmod 0600, close+unlink on stop.
   - ticket: issue() makes secrets.token_urlsafe​(18) current; revoke() is async: sets it None AND waits for any in-flight call
     to finish (acquire the call lock), so nothing runs after revocation.
   - Protocol: request = ONE JSON line {"ticket": str, "argv": [str, ...], "stdin": str|null}, max 2 MiB, read timeout 15 s;
     response = ONE JSON line {"code": int, "output": str}. At most 4 concurrent connections (extra ones get an error and close).
     Calls are serialized by one asyncio.Lock (engine writes are not concurrent-safe).

     this turn went to the VPS master and to stop and wait for the next event.
   - Ops (argv[0]): "status" -> JSON text {table, campaign, turn, ticket_ok}; "prompt" -> contents of <sdir>/gm-system-prompt.md
     (the driver builds it, see build_prompt); "read <relpath>" -> a UTF-8 text file inside world-state/campaigns/<campaign>/
     (resolve(), must stay inside, regular file, <= 256 KiB, no symlink escape); otherwise a tool.
   - Tool: drop a leading "bash"; accept "tools/dm-x.sh" or "dm-x.sh"; name must match ^dm-[a-z0-9-]+\.sh$ and exist as

     wait|enable|speak|audition|key, dm-screen.sh audio make|add|seed, dm-screen.sh voice design|keep|delete|model,
     dm-campaign.sh switch|create|import|reset|delete (and any other destructive subcommand you find in that tool),
     dm-play.sh anything except "status". Args: no NUL, total <= 64 KiB; stdin <= 1 MiB.

   - tool_env = the same variables the SDK master's tools see: os.environ (already scrubbed by the driver) plus DM_ACTIVE_CAMPAIGN,
